one_liner: C++17 RFC 3986-style URL splitter with Public Suffix List domain extraction; its own parse+accessor loop runs ~1.25x ahead of ada.
what_it_does: Splits a URL into scheme, userinfo, host, port, path, params, query and fragment. It classifies the host as hostname, IPv4 or IPv6 (a std::variant), and splits a hostname into subdomain, domain and suffix with an embedded Public Suffix List, which ada does not offer. The API is its own: urlparser::url(std::string_view) throws std::invalid_argument on bad input and exposes string_view accessors such as protocol(), host_text(), query() and fragment(), plus abspath() and normalized(). The same classes ship as a nanobind Python module (PyPI 'liburlparser') and a 'python -m liburlparser' CLI.
how_it_is_fast: The url constructor copies every field once into one owned buffer and stores (offset, length) spans, so most accessors are string_view reads with no allocation. It finds '#', '?' and ';' with a compare-and-OR SIMD scan: AVX2 selected at runtime, SSE2 or NEON as the baseline, scalar code otherwise. The ada win comes from abspath(), which used to run a full dot-segment resolver on every call; a cheap path_is_already_normalized() pre-scan now copies clean paths through unchanged and caches the result. PSL lookups use a vendored ankerl::unordered_dense open-addressing map, and the project reports +67-70% on host extraction from that change.
when_to_use: You need registrable-domain and public-suffix splitting (for example 'ee.aut.ac.ir' becomes domain 'aut', suffix 'ac.ir') together with basic URL component splitting in one C++ or Python library.
High-volume log or crawl processing of already-well-formed http(s) URLs, where you read scheme, host, path, query and fragment and do not need WHATWG canonicalization.
Python pipelines that use tldextract, tld or publicsuffix2 for domain extraction. The README (2022 run) reports 1.12 s for 10M hosts, against 29.23 s for tldextract and 1.50 s for PyDomainExtractor.
Code that must treat IPv4 and IPv6 hosts as typed addresses with integer conversion and arithmetic, not as domain names.
when_not_to_use: You need WHATWG URL Standard behavior (browser-equivalent parsing, percent-encoding of components, host validation, special-scheme rules). ada and its ports implement the standard. liburlparser is not documented as WHATWG-conformant, and its url constructor only trims, splits and lowercases the scheme and host.

You need the benchmarked speed from a released package. The abspath() fast path and cache landed on master on 2026-09-18. Tag v2.0.0 (2026-09-11), which is also the latest PyPI release, still has the old abspath() that returns std::string by value. That old build measured 0.90-0.91x of ada.
Input that is often messy or relative (dot-segments, repeated slashes, Unicode hosts). The published speed figures come from clean, simple URLs, where the fast path always applies.

Several threads reading one url or hostname object at the same time. The const accessors fill mutable caches (host_cache_, abspath_cache_, hostname's parsed fields) with no locking, and the docs do not address this.
Maturity-sensitive production use: 21 stars, one main author, v2.0.0 only weeks old, and daily API-changing commits (for example scp to scp_url renames and merged source files) in September 2026.

integration.dependencies: none at runtime (PSL data embedded at compile time; vendored ankerl::unordered_dense header, MIT). Build needs CMake >= 3.19 and a Python 3 interpreter (find_package REQUIRED). Configure tries to download public_suffix_list.dat and falls back to the tracked copy. The Python module needs nanobind.
integration.min_toolchain: C++17, CMake 3.19+; Python binding: Python >= 3.10 per PyPI metadata (README still says >= 3.8)
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows (CI matrix on ubuntu/macos/windows-latest). SIMD: x86-64 SSE2 baseline with runtime-dispatched AVX2, aarch64 NEON, scalar fallback elsewhere.
integration.thread_safety: PSL singleton is lazily initialized via a function-local static (thread-safe init). No mutex anywhere: psl::load_from_path/load_from_string replace the shared table unguarded, and const accessors on url/hostname write mutable caches, so a shared object is not safe for concurrent reads. Otherwise not documented.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it covers the same 'parse a URL, read components' job, but the API and semantics differ: protocol() has no trailing ':' and query() has no leading '?', while ada's get_protocol() and get_search() include them. Errors are exceptions, not ada::result. There is no WHATWG normalization, href or setters.

gotchas: abspath() and normalized() drop a trailing '/' on non-root paths ('/a/' becomes '/a') and collapse '//' ('/a//b' becomes '/a/b'). The header documents both as deliberate and as different from ada's normalize_url().

url parsing keeps Unicode hosts verbatim (ASCII-only per RFC 3986). Only idna::to_ascii() or url::normalized() convert them to Punycode, so 'café.com' and its xn-- form do not compare equal after a plain parse.

Master still reports URLPARSER_VERSION 2.0.0, but it differs from the v2.0.0 tag (abspath() now returns const std::string& and there are new APIs). You cannot tell the fast and slow builds apart by version number.
License is ambiguous. The README badge and text say MIT, but the LICENSE file is pybind11's BSD-3-Clause text with 'The Pybind Development Team' as copyright holder, and GitHub reports NOASSERTION.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over Ada, ada-rs, lucid-url or sorug only when you need Public Suffix List domain and suffix splitting (none of those do it) and RFC 3986-level splitting is enough. When WHATWG-correct parsing or canonical href output matters, use Ada or one of its WHATWG ports.
verified_claims_summary: The author's fair_compare.cpp interleaves old liburlparser, new liburlparser and unmodified ada::parse<ada::url_aggregator> in one process; each op parses one URL and reads 5 components, and the new build did ~7.4-7.8M ops/s against ada's ~6.0-6.1M (1.24-1.29x), while the pre-fix build did 0.90-0.91x. Only 'this machine, 3 runs' is stated (no CPU, compiler or flags), urls.txt is not shipped (probably the benchmarks/ corpus of 10k Majestic domains in four simple, clean-path shapes), and ada's side also does WHATWG validation and normalization, so the two sides do not do equal work.
status_note: Actively developed (near-daily commits through 2026-09-25) and small enough to vendor as one .cpp/.h pair, but the benchmarked fast path is on master only (not in v2.0.0 or on PyPI) and the MIT vs BSD-3-Clause license question should be settled before you copy it.
